english: For $x\ge 0$, let $\theta_x$ denote the radian measure of the angle subtended at the centre of a circle of radius $\dfrac{40}{\pi}$ cm by an arc of length $x$ cm of the circle. Let $f:[0,\infty)\to\mathbb{R}$ be defined by $f(x)=\sin^{2}(x^{\circ})+\left|\cos\theta_x\right|$, where $x^{\circ}$ denotes an angle of $x$ degrees. Then the fundamental period of $f$ is ______.
hindi: $x\ge 0$ के लिए, माना $\theta_x$ उस कोण की रेडियन माप है जो $\dfrac{40}{\pi}$ cm त्रिज्या वाले वृत्त के $x$ cm लम्बाई के चाप द्वारा वृत्त के केन्द्र पर अंतरित होता है। माना $f:[0,\infty)\to\mathbb{R}$, $f(x)=\sin^{2}(x^{\circ})+\left|\cos\theta_x\right|$ द्वारा परिभाषित है, जहाँ $x^{\circ}$ का अर्थ $x$ अंश का कोण है। तब $f$ का मूल आवर्तकाल ______ है।
solution: Arc $=r\theta$: $\theta_x=\dfrac{x}{40/\pi}=\dfrac{\pi x}{40}$; $|\cos t|$ has period $\pi$, so $\left|\cos\dfrac{\pi x}{40}\right|$ has period $40$

A period $T$ of $f$ must be a period of each part: the first part contains only the frequency of $\cos\dfrac{\pi x}{90}$, the second only those of $\cos\dfrac{2k\pi x}{40}$, and none of these equals $\dfrac{\pi}{90}$ ($k=\dfrac{2}{9}$ is not an integer), so no cancellation is possible
solution_full: Degree to radian: $x^{\circ}=\dfrac{\pi x}{180}$ radian. Hence $\sin^{2}(x^{\circ})=\dfrac{1-\cos(2x^{\circ})}{2}=\dfrac12-\dfrac12\cos\dfrac{\pi x}{90}$, whose fundamental period is $\dfrac{2\pi}{\pi/90}=180$ (half of the period $360$ of $\sin(x^{\circ})$).
An arc of length $l$ on a circle of radius $r$ subtends $\theta=\dfrac{l}{r}$ radian at the centre. So $\theta_x=\dfrac{x}{40/\pi}=\dfrac{\pi x}{40}$.
$\cos\dfrac{\pi x}{40}$ has period $80$, but $|\cos t|$ has fundamental period $\pi$, so $\left|\cos\dfrac{\pi x}{40}\right|$ has fundamental period $\dfrac{\pi}{\pi/40}=40$.

Write $f=u+v$ with $u(x)=\sin^{2}(x^{\circ})$ and $v(x)=\left|\cos\dfrac{\pi x}{40}\right|$. If $f(x+T)=f(x)$ for all $x\ge0$, then $u(x+T)-u(x)=v(x)-v(x+T)$. The left side is a combination of $\cos\dfrac{\pi x}{90}$ and $\sin\dfrac{\pi x}{90}$; the right side, like $v$, repeats every $40$. A non-zero combination of $\cos\dfrac{\pi x}{90}$, $\sin\dfrac{\pi x}{90}$ does not repeat every $40$ (that would need $\dfrac{40}{180}$ to be an integer), so both sides are $0$: $T$ is a period of $u$ and of $v$.
Hence $T$ is a common multiple of $180$ and $40$, and the least one is $\mathrm{LCM}(180,40)=360$. Indeed $f(x+360)=f(x)$, as $360=2\cdot180=9\cdot40$.
Therefore the fundamental period of $f$ is $360$.
originality_note: New: one term uses an angle in degrees and the other an angle defined by an arc of a circle whose radius contains pi, so the two measures must be converted to the same variable before the periods (each halved by a square or a modulus) are combined (way 5). Closest known: period of sin(x degrees) or of |sin x| + |cos x|-type sums. Different because: the radian measure comes from arc = r theta with r = 40/pi, and both halvings (square and modulus) affect the LCM (720 without them).
stem_review: Read as a student: every symbol, function and domain introduced, conditions complete, one reading of each sentence; answer recomputed with sympy/numpy and unique; answer matches the plan. Domain [0, infinity) chosen because an arc length is non-negative; checked numerically that 360 is the least period on [0, 2000]. Changed: No change.
key_step: Convert x degrees and the arc-length angle to pi x/180 and pi x/40, halve both periods (square, modulus), then LCM(180, 40) = 360.
justification: Several routine conversions (degree to radian, arc = r theta) followed by two period-halving traps and an LCM, with no options; each step is standard, but the chain and the traps put it at the Advanced average for a numerical. Comparable to 2026-P1-Q4 (L2, angle conversion with range shift) plus the period combination, so placed one level above it.

concept_use.Periodic functions: fundamental period: Fundamental periods 180 of sin^2(x degrees) and 40 of |cos(pi x/40)|, combined by LCM into 360 after showing no cancellation.
concept_use.Measurement of angles: degree, radian, a: x degrees = pi x/180 radian, and the arc-length relation theta = l/r with r = 40/pi gives theta_x = pi x/40.
